text_post: A few weeks back, she scheduled a wonderfully transparent and to-the-point out-of-the-office auto-reply to her team notifying them that she’d be gone for a few days to care for her mental health. I’d like to be able to take Thursday to Monday off also. You know she just popped up to the cottage. I’ve seen this a thousand times. Oh, “my daughter was sick” so they take the day off, their friends are going up to the cottage lets pull a couple of sick days and head up for “mental health” reasons. “I had a dentist appointment on Wednesday so I may as well make a long weekend of it because I’m stressed’. People take jobs that require evening hours (ie:12-8) and then go on disability for stress because they need to be home with their kids in the evening, eventually ending up at a human rights council cause after a few months there bosses wanted them to go back to work. So while I’m all for mental health days and don’t wish to make light of actual mental health problems these breaks for people who just don’t feel like going to work add up to millions of days of work lost per year and hundreds of billions of dollars. but a person in the midst of a debilitating anxiety attack or trying to keep their head above water during a depressive episode will likelier suck it up, show up, and try to keep going, no matter how ugly life feels at that moment. That’s blatantly false. People are notorious for not sucking it up . At least in the country where I live. Nobody who even has a sniffle shows up to work.

I have been feeling like that many times in the last decades. But: Contract is contract, and work will not do itself, and the computer cannot do all instead of me. And, I always had slightly flexible work time, the only demand being that the job has to be done well and in time, and be there when they need me. So it did not matter if I slept enough in the morning and drank a few more coffees to be more productive through the day, and being longer time in the office or lab (in case of s~~~load of work, until 22+’o clock PM,some pubs were already closed, no beer on the way home). I had depression or bad mood sometimes, or s~~~ was boring because there were half a dozen projects running and bottlenecked by something I cannot have control on, and then many stuff could be continued all at once and deadlines approaching and I don’t know what to start with. And even if many days are like that, I never took “sick” days for mental stuff, When I had flu I worked from home (by remote desktop) what was possible, my only “sick” days were when they pulled out my wisdom-teeth and it took a long time for the dentist and hurt a lot afterwards. Although I took them also from regular holidays instead of sick days, so no need for stupid paperworks. When I am mentally tired, I take regular holidays. In my country we have like 20 workdays or more for older people. That’s more than enough for everything. So to conclude, if work has to be done, it has to be done even if you are tired, because that is what they pay you for, and this woman did not understand that.
